# The phases, step by step

`npm run heldout -- advance KEY` runs these in order and names the subagent each one needs (`heldout drive KEY` also
starts each one, headlessly, in Claude Code). Read this when a step needs a closer look, or when you run one by hand.
`H="npm run heldout --"` (in Windows PowerShell, `npm run heldout '--' …`).

| # | Phase | You do | Command / output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Fetch** | Pull the story's title, description and acceptance criteria, the screenshots they show and the Confluence pages they link (comments and other attachments are not requirement), into the folder of its AUT profile. A re-fetch detects requirement revisions | `$H fetch KEY [--aut <profile>]` → `1-requirement/` (+ `CHANGES.md`, `revisions/`) |
| 1b | **Contract** | `$H contract KEY --pack`, then **delegate** the building to the `heldout-contract-extractor` subagent. From the evidence pack it writes: each AC verbatim with cited lines; rules, endpoints, error cases, auth and test data; **gaps**, each either *mechanics* (HOW: left open, discovered in phase 3) or *oracle* (WHAT: found in the requirement, otherwise left open or assumed for the verdict to report); a coverage ledger for every source line; and each criterion's **checks**, every expected value cited. Then delegate an **independent review** to the `heldout-contract-reviewer` subagent, in a fresh context. Send findings back to the builder and re-review until `$H contract KEY` is clean (after 2 rounds, what is still disputed becomes an open question). **Don't ask the user** the open oracle questions it lists: they go to the tests and the verdict | `2-contract/contract.json`, `2-contract/review.json` — [requirement-contract](requirement-contract.md) |
| 2 | **Generate the tests** | `advance` does it: `$H scaffold KEY` writes the spec from the reviewed contract's checks, one test a check (one per row of a check with rows), tagged with its `@AC-n`, its `@type` and a `// from` source, its steps in the contract's words and empty (`// TODO(harden)`), each expectation as `expectCheck('C3.1.a', actual)`. No expected value is in the spec: the contract is its only place | `3-tests/<key>.spec.ts`, `3-tests/test-data.json` — [requirement-contract](requirement-contract.md), "Checks" |
| 3 | **Freeze, then make them run** | `advance` freezes the draft with the contract's oracle (and a hash of each journey it uses): `$H integrity KEY --snapshot`. The draft stays as frozen in `3-tests/`; the operator gets its own copy in `4-hardening/`, the tests that run. Then **delegate** to the `heldout-operator` ("Make the tests of KEY run"). It makes the steps work against the live AUT with the browser and API tiers, in the tests and the journeys they call, resolves the open mechanics gaps (`discovered-in-aut`, which changes no reviewed content), saves an accounts recipe when the story needs users, proves stability with `$H run KEY --label harden --repeat-each 3 --workers 2`, and goes on into the evaluation run and the triage by itself. When it reports a check that can't be right, send it to the extractor ("Correct check C… of KEY: …"), have the contract reviewed again, generate the tests again and re-freeze with a reason | `3-tests/freeze.json`, `4-hardening/` (the tests that run, `hardening.md`, the probes it cites) — [hardening](hardening.md) |
| 4 | **Run** | `advance` runs the full suite. Preflight (lint, contract and review, journeys, 3-sample healthcheck) runs automatically; a down or **degraded** AUT aborts the run (`--allow-degraded` overrides) | `$H run KEY --label eval` → `5-run/NN-eval.json` |
| 5 | **Triage** | `advance` classifies the failures and replays the sure API ones outside the test (`$H triage KEY --replay`); the `heldout-operator` reproduces the rest live and records each decision with evidence, never editing a test while it triages. Send the script defects it confirms back to it ("Repair these script defects for KEY: …"), then `$H advance KEY --rerun` (the triage carries decisions over with `--carry-from auto`). At most 3 cycles in a row | `6-triage/decisions.json`, the cited live reports in `6-triage/` — [triage](triage.md) |
| 6 | **Verify** | `advance` reproduces each finding once more: a replayed one stands; the others' tests run again on their own, and one that doesn't fail the same way is recorded as NEEDS_INVESTIGATION | `$H verify KEY` → `6-triage/verification.json` |
| 7 | **Verdict** | Render the recommendation with traceability, reproduction and evidence, and the test catalogue: every check in plain words, its result and how to run it again | `$H verdict KEY` → `7-verdict/verdict.md`, `verdict.json`, `catalogue.md` — [verdict-and-publish](verdict-and-publish.md) |
| 8 | **Publish** | Attach the verdict, post a summary comment, set a label. Nothing else. Part of the evaluation, with no confirmation; a project that wants a person to publish sets `jira.publish` to `"manual"`, and `advance` then leaves this step out | `$H publish KEY` |
| 9 | **Journey registry** | Record in `journeys/registry.yml` the journeys this story's passing tests used (this story as their proof, and what ran before each), and the stale marks. Journeys only failing tests used are left out. Commit `registry.yml` with the journey files, `application-map/` and the story's output. After merging other people's work, `$H journeys --check` lints every journey and lists possible duplicates; a merge conflict in `registry.yml` is settled by `$H journeys --resolve` | `$H journeys KEY --harvest` → `--harvest --apply` → `journeys/registry.yml` — [journeys](journeys.md) |
